subject: Clarify evidence window: processing_time vs event_time & EoM inclusivity
messages:
From: Linda Kraus <linda.kraus@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elaine Cho <elaine@brightaudits.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence window question — last day inclusivity for SOC 2 T2

Hi Marissa,

Quick question as we're preparing the evidence packet for Acme's SOC 2 Type II: the control owner is asking whether the 'end of period' for your 2026 coverage should be interpreted as inclusive through 2026-06-30 23:59:59 UTC or whether events with processing_time after that boundary but event_time on/before that boundary are considered in scope.

Specifically: our ingestion logs have both event_time (when the request hit the edge) and processing_time (when the row was written to the replica). For a small subset of sessions the processing_time can roll past midnight UTC while event_time remains on the last day. The auditor wants to know which timestamp Redwood considers authoritative for point-in-time evidence.

Can you confirm:
- Which timestamp do you assert in the SOC 2 report (event_time vs processing_time) as the determinative field for the 'through' moment?
- If processing_time is used, do you have a documented mapping or bridge statement that auditors can rely on?

If convenient, please send a sample of the replica lag export and any wording you would propose for a bridge letter. We need to finalize whether we can rely on your exports as-is or whether we will require an as-of snapshot at 23:59:59 UTC.

Thanks,
Linda
Linda Kraus
Senior Security Engineer | Acme Payments
[attachment: sample-ask.txt]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Linda Kraus <linda.kraus@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Elaine Cho <elaine@brightaudits.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence window question — last day inclusivity for SOC 2 T2

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear examples. Short answer: we treat event_time as authoritative where it exists, but there are a couple of important caveats for the dataset you described.

Details:
- Canonical field: event_time is our canonical 'time-of-occurrence' and is what our SOC 2 evidence ties to when available. Most of the front-door logs and request traces include event_time.
- Processing-only records: certain internal replication/analytics exports only contain processing_time (for example, the read-replica write timestamp). For those exports we do NOT retroactively alter the processing_time; instead we provide a mapping file and a bridge letter that explains how to interpret processing_time relative to event_time.
- Timezone conversions: we store event_time in UTC in our canonical logs. If your auditors ask for a 23:59:59 UTC as-of snapshot, we can generate an as-of export that filters on event_time <= 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z.

Attached: SOC2-T2-2026-report.pdf (redacted PII), and a small replica-lag CSV extract. If you want, I can also attach a draft bridge letter that states: 'Rows with processing_time > cutoff that contain an event_time <= cutoff are considered in-scope because event_time is the canonical field.'

Next steps:
- If BrightAudits will accept event_time as authoritative, we will mark the replica-lag export as supplemental evidence and provide the mapping file.
- If they require an as-of export (filter on event_time), say so and we will produce the filtered snapshot for the requested timestamp.

I've attached the following for your review: SOC2-T2-2026-report.pdf, db-replica-lag-export-202706.csv (sample), bridge-letter-draft.docx.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call if that speeds things up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, InfoSec Programs | Redwood Inference
[attachments: SOC2-T2-2026-report.pdf (PDF, 3.4MB); db-replica-lag-export-202706.csv (CSV, 1.2MB); bridge-letter-draft.docx (DOCX, 45KB)]
From: Elaine Cho <elaine@brightaudits.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Linda Kraus <linda.kraus@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence window question — last day inclusivity for SOC 2 T2

Thanks Marissa — the approach you outlined is reasonable. A couple of clarifying asks from the audit team so we can document it in the report: 

1) Explicit definition we will include in the auditor workpapers: please provide the exact one-line statement you want us to reference. Suggested language is fine.

2) For the as-of option: if we request an as-of export (event_time <= 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z) please confirm whether your extraction pipeline will apply any timezone normalization (we need to know the source timezone for processing_time-derived timestamps).

3) Edge case: there are a limited number of events where event_time is missing and processing_time differs by more than 24 hours (replay/backfill). For those rows, would Redwood be willing to flag them in the CSV with a 'backfilled=true' column and include an explanation in the bridge letter?

If you can provide: (a) the one-line authority statement we can quote, (b) sample CSV with a backfilled column example, and (c) a draft bridge-letter sentence, we can proceed and avoid requesting a full as-of export. If we still need the as-of export we'll let you know, but the flagged/backfilled approach would likely be sufficient for our sampling workpapers.

Regards,
Elaine Cho
Engagement Manager | BrightAudits
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Cho <elaine@brightaudits.com>, Linda Kraus <linda.kraus@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evidence window question — last day inclusivity for SOC 2 T2

Hi Elaine — thanks, that all works. See requested items below.

1) One-line authoritative statement (for workpapers):
"Redwood Inference asserts that event_time is the authoritative timestamp for point-in-time coverage in SOC 2 evidence; when event_time is unavailable, processing_time is provided with an explicit backfilled flag and mapping explanation."

2) Timezone normalization: processing_time values are stored in UTC; our extraction pipeline does not apply additional offsets during export. Your sample CSV will therefore show both event_time (UTC when present) and processing_time (UTC).

3) Backfilled rows: we will add a boolean column named 'backfilled' for rows that were replayed or backfilled after the event_time. For the small population where event_time is missing and processing_time is >24 hours after expected, backfilled=true and we will include a short reason field in the mapped export.

I've attached the draft bridge-letter wording as requested and a 50-row sample of the replica-lag export with a backfilled example row. If that satisfies BrightAudits, no as-of export is necessary. Otherwise let me know and we'll produce an event_time-filtered snapshot at 2026-06-30T23:59:59Z.

If you'd like a quick call to confirm sampling rows and the bridge-letter text, Dylan and I are available tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, InfoSec Programs | Redwood Inference
[attachments: bridge-letter-draft.docx; db-replica-lag-export-202706.csv]
